newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Senegal and European Union near fishing deal.
newsitem.headline: Senegal and European Union near fishing deal.

text.p: Senegal and the European Union are close to renewing a two-year fishing rights deal after failing to agree in November on an EU compensation package, delegates said on Wednesday.
"We have already settled the problem of financial compensation. What is left is technical aspects", said a Senegalese expert.
"I hope this afternoon the protocol will be signed," said another delegate, adding that talks had been extended by one day from Tuesday to deal with technical aspects.
The fifth round of talks on fishing rights between Senegal and the EU opened on Sunday after a previous round collapsed in November on renewing a two-year fishing agreement beyond October 1, 1996.
In previous rounds, Senegal has demanded a payment of 18 million ECUs against 10 million ECUs offered by the EU as compensation in exchange for fishing rights.
A total of 14 EU fishing vessels were in Senegalese waters before the November talks collapsed. Senegal subsequently imposed a fishing ban.
The West African state earned more that 137 billion CFA francs from its fishing industry in 1995. More than 400,000 people are directly or indirectly dependent on the sector.
The European Union gave Senegal 31.2 million ECUs for 1992-94 and 15.8 millions ECUs for 1994-96.

"Many will not understand, after such a long and fruitful cooperation, (the reason for) our talks being deadlocked for so long," Diagua Gueye, head of the Senegalese delegation, said at the start of talks on Sunday.
Senegal was in 1979 the first country to sign such a fishing protocol with the EU.
